title: A Django signal on a Geotrek-class model change is enough to give territorial data attribution and replay
content:
Makina Corpus works in Python and Django daily, and the demo places the dispatch point exactly there: a Django signal fired on a model change in a Geotrek-class application, emitting a typed operation. The mechanism is one of the framework's ordinary extension points, so nothing about the integration is foreign to the team that would maintain it.

What the operation buys is attribution and replay for territorial data. A Django model holds the current value of a field; the dispatched operation records that a change happened, by whom, and in what order relative to everything else, so the state of the dataset at an earlier date can be reconstructed rather than inferred.

Choosing a demo inside a stack the firm already inhabits removes the usual objection to a record layer, which is that it is another technology to learn. Here the seam is a small change in a place their developers already edit, which makes it a plausible first co-built artefact rather than a proof of concept that needs an internal champion to survive.
